objective: A user can edit the project opened in a detail route even when the global project selector points to a different accessible project, without changing that selector.

requirements.statement: For every project-detail request addressed as /api/project/{projectId}, the client must send the same projectId as request context; opening or editing that detail must not change the persisted global project selection.
acceptance: With global selector project A and detail route project B, basic information, plan, and attachment requests use URL project B and X-Project-Id B.
Those requests no longer return the path/context mismatch error.
The global selector remains project A until the user explicitly switches it.
requirements.source: User-confirmed design and implementation plan on 2026-09-18
counterexample: A request to /api/project/B sends X-Project-Id A.
Opening or saving B changes the persisted global selector to B.
The server accepts a missing or mismatched project context.

invariants: The global selector changes only through an explicit selector action.
The server continues enforcing matching project path and X-Project-Id plus existing authorization, tenant, entity, audit, and lock behavior.
Existing API paths, HTTP methods, request bodies, response types, database data, and routes remain compatible.
constraints: Modify only web/src/api/project.ts, web/src/api/attachments.ts, and the current task's authorized evidence files.
Do not modify http.ts, project-context store, server security, services, database, or .env files.
Use local services and synthetic local test data only.
non_goals: Changing global project-switch confirmation or persistence behavior.
Adding an HTTP interceptor inference rule.
Changing API payloads, migrations, permissions, or audit behavior.

assumptions.text: The existing withProjectContext(id) request configuration overrides the stored global project context.
assumptions.basis: http.ts request interceptor selects explicit projectContext before local storage.
assumptions.falsifier: A browser request for detail project B sends X-Project-Id A after the scoped client update.

unknowns.question: The local account may expose fewer than two projects, preventing a full A/B browser scenario.
unknowns.impact: Browser evidence may be limited to static and single-project request checks.

decisions.question: Which project identity controls a project-detail request?
Should server project path/context validation be changed?

measurement_intents.observable: Source request configuration binds each project route ID explicitly and a route B request carries header B while stored selection remains A.
measurement_intents.candidate_sensor: Static API audit, Vite build, browser network headers, browser local-storage state
